# Google Jobs Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/google-jobs-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/google-jobs-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects job listing data from Google Jobs (the `udm=8` vertical on Google Search), written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Google Jobs in 2026](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-google-jobs)
- **Code:** [`google_jobs.py`](google_jobs.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Search](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Google Jobs search results for a given query and location
- Job title, company, location, posted date, schedule type, and salary range
- Job description, qualifications, source board, application URL, and job ID

## Functions

- `scrape_jobs(query, location, language='en', country_code='us', date_filter=None)` → `JobSearch`: Scrape Google Jobs for the given query and location.

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import google_jobs


async def main():
    jobs = await google_jobs.scrape_jobs(query="python developer", location="San Francisco, CA")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`JobResult`**: `title`, `company?`, `location?`, `posted_date?`, `schedule_type?`, `salary_range?`, `description?`, `qualifications`, `source_board?`, `application_url?`, `job_id?`
- **`JobSearch`**: `query`, `location`, `search_date`, `jobs`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`google_jobs.py`](google_jobs.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/google-jobs-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
